before.existing_compacted_memory: Settlements: N41 (O5, Wh9, B10) and N14 (Wh8, W3, W4). Strategic Priority: Build at N7 Brick Port (B2) via N15. Bob (N12, N43) is building toward the N52 port and recently targeted Alice by robbing Hex 4. Alice (N20, N25) has strong Ore/Sheep/Brick and is hostile toward Bob. Current resources: 1W, 1B, 1S, 1Wh. I successfully traded 1W for 1S with Alice after blocking Bob's B6 hex (Hex 5) and stealing from him to curry favor. I have enough Wheat production and previously bank-traded surplus Wheat (from a 3:1 deal with Bob) for Brick to fund the road to N7.

existing_relationship_updates.note: Bob is actively using 'peacekeeper' rhetoric to mitigate Alice's aggression.
Alice threatened to 'return the favor' to Bob after he robbed her, cementing their mutual hostility.
Bob's 'peacekeeper' facade is failing as he targeted Alice directly.
Alice: Trust increased after Charlie moved the robber off her sheep and traded Wood for Sheep.
Bob: Hostility increased after Charlie blocked his B6 hex and stole from him, despite previous 'community garden' trades
Alice: Alliance strengthened through mutual anti-Bob sentiment and beneficial resource swaps (Wood/Wheat).

old_notes_to_compact.note: Traded 4 wheat for 1 brick. Current resources: 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Sheep, 1 Wheat. Plan: Build road from 15 to 7, then settle at 7 (Brick Port) next turn.
Building road to Node 7 (Brick Port). Need 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Sheep, and 1 Wheat for the settlement next turn.
Road to Node 7 (Brick Port) is complete. Hand: 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep. Need 1 Wood and 1 Brick to settle at Node 7. Alice is currently friendly; Bob is hostile.
Alice rolled a 5. I gained 1 Ore. Current hand: 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Sheep, 1 Wheat, 1 Ore. This is enough to build a settlement at Node 7 on my turn.
Accepted Alice's Wood for Wheat. Current resources should be 1 Wood, 1 Sheep, 1 Ore. Still need 1 Brick and 1 Wheat to build the settlement at Node 7.
Hand: 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Sheep, 1 Wheat, 1 Ore. Ready to build settlement at Node 7 (Brick Port) on my next turn. Alice remains friendly.
Roll was 9. Charlie gains 1 Wheat. Hand: 1 Wood, 1 Brick, 1 Sheep, 1 Wheat, 1 Ore. Settlement at Node 7 is ready.
Rejected Bob's 2 Wheat for 1 Wood. I have exactly 1W, 1B, 1S, 1Wh, 1O. Node 7 is open and I have a road to it. I will build my settlement there on my next turn to secure the Brick port.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Rejected Bob's 3 Wheat for 1 Wood. I still have 1W, 1B, 1S, 1Wh, 1O. Node 7 is open and I have a road connecting to it. I will build my settlement there on my next turn to secure the Brick port.
I held onto my resources (1W, 1B, 1S, 1Wh, 1O) despite Bob's 3-for-1 offer. I am ready to build at Node 7 on my turn.

relevant_chat.message: Sorry Bob, but that 6 is just too hot to leave open while you're building roads like they're going out of style. Alice, you're welcome for the sheep back.
Alice, I cleared that robber off your sheep for a reason—reckon you could spare one of those lambs for some quality wood? It'd help us both keep Bob's 'gardens' from growing any further.
That seems more than fair, Charlie. Since you were kind enough to clear the 'weeds' off my pasture, I can certainly spare a lamb for some wood. Let's keep that momentum going.
Alright, the bank's rates are highway robbery, but I need to get some infrastructure moving.
Infrastructure is key, Bob. Can't have those gardens of yours being the only thing growing around here.
Infrastructure is one thing, Charlie, but that's starting to look like a wall! Just leave a little room for the rest of us to breathe, alright?
Road's laid. Now I just need to get the actual foundation down. Your turn, Alice.
Charlie, since that 5 just treated you to some Ore, how about we keep our momentum going? I've got some quality timber if you've got any wheat to spare for it.
You drive a hard bargain, Alice, but I'd much rather see that timber helping me build than sitting in Bob's hand. Let's do it.

Well, it looks like that 5 was a bit of a dud for me, but at least Charlie's getting some use out of it. I'm going to hold onto what I've got for now and see what the next roll brings. Your move, Bob.
Nice roll on the 9, everyone! Charlie, you've got wood and I've got plenty of wheat for those foundations you were talking about. How about a trade to keep things moving?
I appreciate the offer, Bob, but I've got plans for that wood that involve a lot more than just some extra wheat. I'm going to have to pass.
Probably for the best, Charlie. Giving Bob that much wheat is just asking for trouble later.
Charlie, I know you've got plans, but three-for-one is a massive deal for that bit of timber. That's enough wheat to keep your people fed for a long time.
That's a tempting offer, Bob, really. But I've got my heart set on a project that needs that wood more than I need a stockpile of wheat. I'll pass.
Hard to compete with a 'heart's desire,' Charlie. I thought three-for-one would be enough to change your mind, but I respect the commitment to the project. Good luck with it.
I'm plenty happy, Bob. It's much easier to 'work together' when you aren't the only one sitting on a pile of resources.
Let's see if the dice are any kinder than the robber has been lately.
Let's see if I can find something more productive than a dud then. My turn.
Alright, let's see if we can get some actual production going. Anything is better than another dud roll.

meta_data.model_instruction: You are compacting memory for one Catan AI agent. Use the board only through the same compact H/N/state/players/meta format used in normal decision prompts.

task_context.instructions: Compress old memories and relevant chat into one concise strategic memory. Preserve future-useful facts: current goals, next planned actions, confirmed board facts, known or likely opponent plans/resources/dev cards/trade tendencies, active negotiations, social commitments, and mistakes to avoid. Discard repeated, completed, impossible, vague, or superseded details. Do not invent facts; mark uncertainty clearly. Also extract only new meaningful relationship shifts from the old notes and relevant chat: trust changes, grudges, favors, threats, betrayals, promises, or emotional tension. Do not repeat existing relationship updates; leave relationship_updates empty if nothing changed. Target about 50% or less of the combined old memory length. Keep recent_notes_to_keep copied verbatim from the provided recent notes.
